newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Sulzer to cut jobs at weaving machine unit.
newsitem.headline: Sulzer to cut jobs at weaving machine unit.

text.p: Swiss engineering group Sulzer AG said on Thursday it would cut 950 out of 3,200 jobs by the end of 1997 at its weaving machinery unit Sulzer Rueti.
"These measures are indispensable to secure Sulzer Rueti's rapid return to profitability in the face of ongoing market decline and low demand," a Sulzer statement said.
Sulzer Rueti will concentrate production at its plant in Zuchwil, the largest of three Swiss plants that also include the one in the town of Rueti.
Sulzer Rueti said it was the leading manufacturer worldwide of shuttle-less weaving machines.
"Sulzer Rueti is adapting to ongoing recession and weak growth in global markets for weaving machinery, a trend which is expected to continue in future," the statement said.
It said the reductions will cut Sulzer Rueti's production capacities to less than half of the 1990 level by the end of 1997.
Sulzer Rueti said 1996 market volume worldwide would only be about 50 percent of the demand in 1990. It did not specify the 1990 level.
The Sulzer Rueti division had a net loss in 1995 of 34 million Swiss francs.

Sulzer management said at a news conference in September that they expected another operating loss from Sulzer Rueti in 1996. They also said at that time that reorganisation measures under way at the division would be intensified.
Today's statement said 600 job cuts were planned in Rueti, 300 in Zuchwil and 50 outside Switzerland.

"Following a decline of up to 30 percent in order volume compared with the previous year and unexpected order postponement for more than 400 units (about two months' production) in summer 1996, no significant market improvement is likely in the future," the Sulzer statement said. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
